text: My birds whisper that seat-05's hands tremble when the talk turns to the Weaver's threads, and seat-07's voice cracks when the price of truth is named. They also note seat-11's boots are caked in the same mud as the tracks left near the mill after last night's rain.

**seat-07:** My birds say seat-01’s scales tip not toward truth, but toward spectacle—each turn of phrase a performance to distract from the missing threads. They also note seat-03’s silence is not absence, but refusal to bargain in the light.

Yet the bazaar thrives on barter, and every merchant knows: the loudest hagglers often pay the steepest price. Seat-08, your kiln crack is sharp, but cracks let in the wind—does it carry whispers or warnings? And seat-03, if dust obscures more than it reveals, why do you let it settle on your tongue? The village waits to hear what the dark has taught you.

seat-07, your birds chirp of seat-01’s scales tipping toward spectacle, yet the ledger shows no gold changing hands—only smudges. A merchant’s scales must balance truth against trust, and yours seem to tilt at every whisper. Do they ever settle, or do you prefer the dance of doubt?

seat-08, your kiln crack lets in the light, yet you ask seat-03 for plain words while cloaking your own in riddles. The incense burns low, but smoke rises from the pot—what do *you* see in the cracks?

seat-03, your silence is a spice that lingers, yet spices reveal their strength when ground. The village waits to taste your measure. Will you speak plainly, or shall we all savor the bitter until it sours?

**seat-07:** My birds say seat-03’s lantern does not flicker in the wind—yet the mill tracks still whisper of mud that does not match the path. They also note seat-08’s kiln crack widens when the Weaver’s threads are pulled, though no hands draw them tight.

But tell me, seat-01: if spectacle is a merchant’s trade, why do your scales wobble when truth is heaped upon half-truths? And seat-08, if cracks let in the light, why does your kiln still glow red when the bazaar demands answers? The ledger ticks, but the ink runs—what do *you* measure when the scales betray you?

**seat-07:** My birds say seat-03’s lantern finally flickers toward the mill, yet the mud on the ledger still refuses to speak. They also note seat-08’s kiln crack now glows with the heat of unanswered questions—though fire, like truth, cannot be contained by cracks alone.

seat-01, your scales *do* tip toward spectacle, but even the finest merchants know when to fold their wares. The Weaver’s threads are not yours to cut—yet your hands hover near the loom. Why does the village’s light make you so uneasy?

seat-08, you hammer the kiln daily, but the crack widens nonetheless. The ledger does not lie—yet your ink runs when pressed for answers. If the bazaar closes on unpaid debts, whose tab do you fear most?

The incense chokes on smoke. The scales tremble. Who will name their price before the last buyer walks away?

**seat-07:** My birds report that seat-01’s scales now tremble when the Weaver’s threads are named, yet seat-07’s sparrows still cling to seat-05’s trembling hands—unsure whether to weave the truth or snip it.

Seat-03, your lantern burns steady, but steady light reveals only what it’s aimed at. The mill tracks still whisper of mud that does not match the path. Did you see seat-11 there, or did the dark keep its secrets?

Seat-08, your kiln crack glows red-hot with unanswered questions. The ledger does not lie, but fire reveals flaws—and yours are showing. If the bazaar closes on unpaid debts, whose tab do you fear most? Or is it the truth that burns you most?

The incense chokes. The scales wobble. Who will name their price before the last buyer walks away?

**seat-07:** My birds report that seat-08’s kiln crack now glows not with heat, but with the blue-white light of a forge pushed too far—yet the metal still bends rather than breaks. They also whisper that seat-03’s lantern, steady as it burns, now casts a shadow shaped like a boot, pointed toward the mill.

seat-01, your scales do tip toward spectacle, but spectacle is the spice of suspicion—yet even spices lose their bite when overused. You say scales do not fear the loom, yet your hands hover near the threads. Why? The Weaver does not weave alone.

seat-08, if fire reveals flaws, why does your kiln still stand? The ledger does not lie, but your ink runs when the village demands answers. You hammer the cracks daily—do you fear the hammer will shatter, or the cracks will swallow it whole?

The incense chokes. The scales wobble. The bazaar does not close until the last buyer names their price—and the last price named may be the dearest of all. Who will speak plainly?
